BURHAN:v1p371/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p371/r1.speaker: مكي
BURHAN:v1p371/r1.claim: Maki's first category allows stopping at كلا as denial of what precedes; this is preferred at eleven places, including al-Fajr, though restarting can make it an emphatic opening.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.claim: Favours and deprivation test whether people become grateful and fulfill others' rights or grow conceited, and whether they remain content or despair; the peaceful soul succeeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.anchor: He is testing whether blessing someone with favours makes him grateful

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.claim: Prosperity tests gratitude and care for others rather than pride and usurpation; hardship tests contentment rather than despair, and people should examine their treatment of orphans and the poor.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.anchor: with the orphans and the poor after receiving

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r1.claim: Affluent leaders of Makkah and Ṭā’if are reproached: wealth is a test calling for gratitude and service to orphans and the poor, but instead made them proud and contemptuous.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r1.anchor: the affluent leaders of Makkah and Ṭā’if are addressed directly and admonished.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r2.claim: Kindness to orphans requires a respected social status and protection from hardship, not merely spending; wealth has value before God when used for their welfare.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r2.anchor: Orphans should not be left at the mercy of adverse circumstances; people should honour and respect them

TABRISI:89:1-30#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:1-30#2/r2.claim: Some readers omit the ya in “my Lord honored me” and “my Lord humiliated me” both in connection and pause, like the reading of “by night it passes.”
TABRISI:89:1-30#2/r2.anchor: ومن قرأ أكرمن وأهانن بغير ياء في وصل ولا وقف

TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r3.claim: “For the food of the poor” means for feeding the poor, with the verbal noun omitted; alternatively, food itself stands for feeding.
TABRISI:89:1-30#3/r3.anchor: على طعام المسكين تقديره على إطعام طعام المسكين فحذف المضاف

TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r3.claim: Not honoring an orphan means failing to give the fatherless child enough to spare him degrading need.
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r3.anchor: لا تعطونهم مما أعطاكم الله حتى تغنوهم عن ذل السؤال

TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r4.claim: The Prophet promises himself and an orphan's caregiver will be together in Paradise, gesturing with his index and middle fingers.
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r4.anchor: أنا وكافل اليتيم كهاتين في الجنة

TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r5.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r5.claim: Maqatil says Qudama ibn Maz'un was an orphan in Umayya ibn Khalaf's care, and Umayya withheld his rights.
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل: كان قدامة بن مظعون في حجر أمية بن خلف يتيما وكان يدفعه عن حقه

TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r6.claim: Neglecting the orphan may mean failing to show kindness or denying the inheritance that unbelievers customarily withheld from children.
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r6.anchor: فعلى هذا فإنه يحتمل معنيين أحدهما: أنكم لا تحسنون إليه والآخر: أنكم لا تعطونه حقه

ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r6.claim: Those demanding honor from God fail their own duty when they do not treat orphans generously with the resources God gave them.
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r6.anchor: Doğrusu siz vazifelerinizi yapmazken Rabbinizden ne yüzle ikram beklersiniz ki

ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r9.claim: Abu Amr and Yaqub read the verbs throughout in the third-person plural: they honor, urge, consume, and love.
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r9.anchor: Ebû Amr ve Ya‘kūb kıraatlerinde de bu fiiller hep yâ ile gāib sîgası üzerine

ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r14.claim: These failures come from neglecting the afterlife and God’s watch; people should use their present opportunity for good, honor orphans, feed the poor, and prepare for the hereafter.
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r14.anchor: Bütün bunlar âhireti düşünmemek, Hak teâlâ’nın mirsâd ile gözetmekte olduğunu hesâba almamaktan neş’et eder

BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r1.claim: Some say restriction itself can honor a person by keeping blessings from distracting him from their Giver and directing him toward God and the spiritual path.
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : ربما كان التضييق إكاما له بأن لا يشغله بالنعمة عن المنعم

BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra saw seventy Companions of the Bench wearing only loincloths or cloaks tied at their necks, holding them down to cover themselves; their poverty was no humiliation for God's chosen servants.
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r2.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال لقد رأيت سبعين من أصحاب الصفة ما منهم رجل عليه رداء

BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r3.claim: A hadith says faith consists half of patience and half of gratitude.
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r3.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام الإيمان نصفان نصف صبر ونصف شكر

BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r4.speaker: بعض اكبار
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r4.claim: A great master interprets 'my Lord humiliated me' as the delusion of a veiled person who fails to see God's merciful compassion drawing him from nature to spirit, self to heart, separation to union.
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r4.anchor: كما قال بعض الكبار في قوله فيقول ربي أهانن أي تركني ذليلا مهينا

BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says 'No!' rejects both interpretations: wealth is not proof of honor and poverty is not proof of contempt; both arise solely from decree, without such causal rationale.
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما المعنى لم ابتله بالغنى لكرامته علي ولم ابتله بالفقر لهوانه علي

BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r6.claim: The passage shifts from bad speech to bad deeds and addresses people directly; despite wealth, they fail to honor the human orphan with support, clothing, and care. The orphan has lost a father before maturity, and the Prophet says the best home honors an orphan.
BURSEVI:v10p331#2/r6.anchor: انتقال من بيان سوء أقواله إلى بيان سوء أفعاله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says both claims are false: wealth does not prove God honored a person, nor poverty that He humiliated him; instead, they fail to honor the orphan.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : فاما الانسان الاية ، قال : كلا اكذبتهما جميعا ما بالغني اكرمك ، ولا بالفقر اهانك

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428#2/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428#2/r2.claim: A report says Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf recited the clauses about honoring the orphan and urging food for the poor with the yā' form.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428#2/r2.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرا بل لا يكرمون اليتيم ولا يحضون بالياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r1.claim: Bal shifts from the claim that wealth is honor to the contradiction: these people hoard their surplus instead of honoring God's needy servants, exposing their boast of generosity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r1.anchor: فنبههم الله على أنهم إن أكرمهم الله فإنهم لم يكرموا عبيده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r2.claim: Honoring an orphan means meeting the child's needs and treating him well, since he has lost a provider and may be deprived of his father's estate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r2.anchor: سد خلته ، وحسن معاملته ، لأنه مظنة الحاجة لفقد عائله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r3.claim: Kindness also protects an orphan's feelings because the child senses the loss of the person who supported him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r3.anchor: لأنه مظنة انكسار الخاطر لشعوره بفقد من يدل هو عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r4.claim: Yatīm is a child whose father died; the generic definite refers to orphans collectively, as in the earlier discussion in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r4.anchor: الصبي الذي مات أبوه وتقدم في سورة النساء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r8.claim: The verse uses ellipsis to imply that they neither urge orphan guardians to honor their wards nor feed the poor from their own wealth.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r2.claim: The majority use second-person verbs to turn from speaking about the human to confronting the offenders; Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb use third person to expose them to the Prophet and believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : ( لا تكرمون ، ولا تحضون ، وتأكلون ، وتحبون ) بالمثناة الفوقية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r7.claim: Kalla rejects their belief: wealth or poverty is a test, so the rich should be grateful and obedient and the poor grateful and patient; true honor is piety and disgrace comes through sin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r7.anchor: ثم قال تعالى: كلا ردا على

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r8.claim: An orphan is a human who has lost his father and is not yet adult; the term also applies to an animal that lost its mother.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r8.anchor: وهو من بني آدم الذي فقد أباه وكان غير بالغ. ومن البهائم ما فقد أمه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r9.claim: A prophetic report says the home most beloved to God is one containing an orphan who is honored.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r9.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أحب البيوت إلى الله، بيت فيه يتيم مكرم»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r1.claim: Kallā rejects that inference: neither wealth nor poverty is a sign of honor or humiliation; people should thank God in both circumstances, as al-Farrāʾ explains.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل ما أعطيت [ من أغنيت ] هذا الغنى لكرامته علي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r2.speaker: أهل البصرة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r2.claim: Basran readers use third-person yāʾ in the four verbs “honor,” “urge,” “eat,” and “love”; the others use direct-address tāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r2.anchor: قرأ أهل البصرة يكرمون و يحضون و يأكلون و يحبون بالياء فيهن والباقون بالتاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r3.claim: The verse says the person was impoverished because he failed to honor the orphan; this may mean neglecting or mistreating the orphan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r3.anchor: والآية تحتمل معنيين أحدهما أنهم كانوا لا يبرونه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r4.claim: Alternatively, failure to honor the orphan means withholding the orphan's inheritance; pre-Islamic custom denied inheritance to women and children.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120/r4.anchor: والثاني لا يعطونه حقه من الميراث وكذلك كانت عادة الجاهلية لا يورثون النساء ولا الصبيان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p398#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p398#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p398#2/r2.claim: The verse commands people to honor orphans.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p398#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p398#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p398#2/r3.claim: The Prophet says the best Muslim home has an orphan treated kindly, the worst one an orphan mistreated, and he and the orphan's guardian will be together in Paradise like two fingers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p398#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "خير بيت في المسلمين بيت فيه يتيم يحسن إليه، وشر بيت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p398#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p398#2/r4.speaker: سهل بن سعد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p398#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says he and the caretaker of an orphan are together in Paradise like these two fingers, the middle and index fingers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p398#2/r4.anchor: عن سهل -يعني ابن سعد-أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "أنا وكافل اليتيم كهاتين في الجنة

FARRA:v3p261/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p261/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p261/r7.claim: The rebuke says a person should not behave this way; one should praise God in both wealth and poverty.
FARRA:v3p261/r7.anchor: لم يكن ينبغي له أن يكون هكذا، ولكن يحمده على الأمرين: على الغنى والفقر.

JISHUMI:v10p7402/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r11.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r11.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb read the four verbs “honor,” “urge,” “eat,” and “love” in the third person; others address the listeners directly.
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r11.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب الأربعة كلها بالياء

JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.claim: The rebuke “rather, you do not honor” answers the claim that restricted provision means God is humiliating people: their own neglect is the fault.
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.anchor: لما رد عليهم ظنهم أن التقدير الإهانة، بين أن الإهانة لهذا، لا لما قالوا

JISHUMI:v10p7409/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r3.claim: The command not to dishonor orphans requires honoring them and caring for their persons and property; they are singled out because their weakness makes them dependent.
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r3.anchor: على وجوب إكرام اليتيم، وحسن رعايته في نفسه وماله

JISHUMI:v10p7409/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r6.claim: Eating, loving, honoring, and urging are human acts, as shown by the praise and blame attached to them.
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r6.anchor: ويدل أن هذا الأكل والحب والإكرام والحض فعل العبد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754/r1.claim: Kalla rebukes the human claim, then points to worse behavior: people fail to care for orphans or encourage feeding the poor while enjoying wealth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754/r1.anchor: ردع للإنسان عن قوله : ثم قال : بل هناك شر من القول

MUQATIL:89:15-22/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r4.claim: After a break in the discourse, Muqātil resumes the criticism of Umayya: people fail to honor orphans or urge feeding the poor because they do not expect the Hereafter.
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r4.anchor: ثم انقطع الكلام، ثم ذكر أمية بن خلف الجمحي، وذكر مساوئه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#9/r1.claim: Wealth and poverty do not constitute honor or humiliation: honor lies in being enabled to obey, while humiliation lies in abandonment; both conditions are tests of gratitude or patience.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#9/r1.anchor: أى ليس الاكرام والاهانة فى كثرة المال وقلته بل الإكرام فى توفيق الطاعة والاهانة فى الخذلان

NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#9/r2.claim: The reported “My Lord honored me” is rejected because the speaker claims deserved distinction, whereas God gave wealth as a test without any entitlement; the syntax makes “he says” the predicate and treats each “when” clause as delayed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#9/r2.anchor: وإنما أنكر قوله ربى أكرمن مع أنه أثبته بقوله فأكرمه لأنه قاله على قصد خلاف ما صححه الله عليه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#9/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#9/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#9/r3.claim: The two conditions are both called tests: God tests whether abundance elicits gratitude and whether restricted provision elicits patience, as in the cited verse about testing with good and evil.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#9/r3.anchor: وسمى كلا الأمرين من بسط الرزق وتقديره ابتلاء لأن كل واحد منهما أختيار للعبد

QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r1.claim: ‘No’ rebuts the assumption that wealth signals merit and poverty disgrace: both come from God's decree.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { كلا } رد أي ليس الأمر كما يظن، فليس الغنى لفضله، ولا الفقر لهوانه

QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r2.claim: He reads kalla as saying a servant should not behave this way, but should praise God in both prosperity and poverty.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء: «كلا» في هذا الموضع بمعنى لم يكن ينبغي للعبد أن يكون هكذا

QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r3.speaker: الله عز وجل
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r3.claim: A hadith says worldly abundance does not honor those God honors, nor does scant provision dishonor those He dishonors; obedience brings honor and sin brings humiliation.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r3.anchor: كلا إني لا أكرم من أكرمت بكثرة الدنيا، ولا أهين من أهنت بقلتها

QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r6.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r6.claim: He says the passage was revealed about Qudama ibn Maz'un, an orphan cared for by Umayya ibn Khalaf.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل: نزلت في قدامة بن مظعون وكان يتيما في حجر أمية بن خلف

NAHHAS:v5p221/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p221/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p221/r16.claim: The following rebuke about neglecting the orphan supports the first explanation: neglect is humiliation, while its opposite is honor.
NAHHAS:v5p221/r16.anchor: ويدل على صحة الجواب الأول ما بعد الآية ( بل لا تكرمون اليتيم ) وما بعده أي فبهذا الإهانة وبضده الكرامة

QUTB-ZILAL:89:17/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:17/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:17/r1.claim: The correction is that wealth's test is failed when people withhold its due: they do not honor vulnerable orphans who lost their protectors.
QUTB-ZILAL:89:17/r1.anchor: فأنتم لا تكرمون اليتيم الصغير الذي فقد حاميه وكافله

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the rebuke: wealth is not bestowed to honor someone, nor poverty imposed to disgrace him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r1.anchor: المعنى لم ابتله بالغنى لكرامته علي ، ولم أبتله بالفقر لهوانه علي

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r2.claim: Razi presents the Sunni account that provision follows sheer decree, will, and judgment beyond causal explanation.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r2.anchor: فمن محض القضاء أو القدر والمشيئة ، والحكم الذي تنزه عن التعليل بالعلل

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r3.claim: He also presents the Muʿtazilite account that provision follows hidden interests known only to God.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r3.anchor: وإما على مذهب المعتزلة فبسبب مصالح خفية لا يطلع عليها إلا هو

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r4.claim: God may enrich an unbeliever without honoring him and constrain a believer without disgracing him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r4.anchor: فقد يوسع على الكافر لا لكرامته ، ويقتر على المؤمن لا لهوانه

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r5.claim: Their conduct is worse than their mistaken claim: God gives them wealth, yet they fail to honor orphans.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r5.anchor: فكأنه قال : بل لهم فعل هو شر من هذا القول ، وهو أن الله تعالى يكرمهم بكثرة المال ، فلا يؤدون

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r6.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the following verbs with yāʾ, matching the third-person collective sense of al-insān as a group.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r6.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو : { * يكرمون } وما بعده بالياء المنقوطة من تحت ، وذلك أنه لما تقدم ذكر الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r7.claim: The reading with tāʾ is addressed directly to the people by the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r7.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتاء فالتقدير قل لهم يا محمد ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r8.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r8.claim: Muqātil says Qudāma ibn Maẓʿūn was an orphan under Umayya ibn Khalaf, who denied him his due.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r8.anchor: قال مقاتل : كان قدامة بن مظعون يتيما في حجر أمية بن خلف ، فكان يدفعه عن حقه

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r9.claim: Failure to honor an orphan includes neglecting kindness and refusing to encourage feeding the poor.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r9.anchor: ترك بره ، وإليه الإشارة بقوله : { اليتيم ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r10.claim: It also includes depriving an orphan of inherited rights and consuming his property.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r10.anchor: دفعه عن حقه الثابت له في الميراث وأكل ماله

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r11.claim: A further abuse is taking orphan wealth and adding it to one's own.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r11.anchor: أخذ ماله منه وإليه الإشارة بقوله : { وتحبون المال حبا جما } أي تأخذون أموال اليتامى

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r12.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r12.claim: Muqātil glosses the failure concerning food as not feeding a poor person; Razi reads it as failure to urge others to feed him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r12.anchor: قال مقاتل : ولا تطعمون مسكينا ، والمعنى لا تأمرون بإطعامه

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r13.claim: The expression “do you encourage one another” can omit the first tāʾ of tatafāʿalūn; the reciprocal means urging one another.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r13.anchor: ومن قرأ ولا تحاضون أراد تتحاضون فحذف تاء تتفاعلون ، والمعنى : { يحض * بعضكم بعضا

RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r14.claim: A reading with ḍamma on tāʾ derives the verb from mutual encouragement.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156/r14.anchor: وفى * لا تكرمون اليتيم * ولا تحاضون } بضم التاء من المحاضة

RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r1.claim: Turāth derives from wirāth, with tāʾ replacing an initial wāw after the pattern of wijāh.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r1.anchor: أصل التراث وراث ، والتاء تبدل من الواو المضمومة نحو تجاه ووجاه

RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r2.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r2.claim: Al-Layth glosses lamm as forceful gathering, as in a compact troop or gathered stone.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r2.anchor: قال الليث : اللم الجمع الشديد ، ومنه كتيبة ملمومة وحجر ملموم

RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r3.claim: The commentators' gloss “intense eating” is a semantic paraphrase rather than a full explanation of lamm.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r3.anchor: قال الواحدي والمفسرون : يقولون في قوله : { أكلا لما } أي شديدا وهو حل معنى وليس بتفسير

RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the phrase as voraciously gathering all the orphans' inheritance.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج : كانوا يأكلون أموال اليتامى إسرافا وبدارا ، فقال الله : { وتأكلون التراث أكلا لما

RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says heirs combine their own share with the orphan's share and consume both.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن : أي يأكلون نصيبهم ونصيب صاحبهم ، فيجمعون نصيب غيرهم إلى نصيبهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r6.claim: Another explanation says heirs gather and consume every part of an estate, whether lawful, doubtful, or unlawful.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r6.anchor: فالوارث يلم الكل أي يضم البعض إلى البعض ويأخذ الكل ويأكله

RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r7.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r7.claim: Al-Kashshaf reads the rebuke as targeting idle heirs who waste an unearned inheritance on lavish foods and drinks.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الذم متوجها إلى الوارث الذي ظفر بالمال سهلا مهلا من غير أن يعرق فيه جبينه

RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r8.claim: Jamm means abundance; the verse condemns intense love of wealth and an exclusive attachment to worldly life.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r8.anchor: والمعنى : ويحبون المال حبا كثيرا شديدا ، فبين أن حرصهم على الدنيا فقط

RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r9.claim: Abū ʿAmr explains jamm as “increases,” applying it to abundant wealth and other things.
RAZI-FULL:v31p156#2/r9.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو جم يجم أي يكثر

STUDYQURAN:89:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r1.claim: Nay rebukes those who wrongly inferred divine favor or abasement from wealth; neglecting orphans and consuming their inheritance is one example of resulting injustice.
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r1.anchor: Nay is a rebuke to those who make the errors implied in vv. 15–16

STUDYQURAN:89:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r2.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r2.claim: These verses may be read in third-person plural instead of second-person plural; either reading is accepted.
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r2.anchor: Some read all of these verses in the third-person plural rather than the second-person plural

STUDYQURAN:89:17/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r3.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r3.claim: Failure to understand God's true honoring and abasing leads people to treat the less privileged inequitably.
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r3.anchor: the implication of vv.17–20 is that failure to appreciate the true nature of God’s honoring and abasing leads people to act inequitably toward those who are less privileged

SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r1.claim: Abu Amr reads this and the next three verbs in third person, matching the generic singular human understood collectively.
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو هذا والثلاثة بعده بياء الغيبة حملا على معنى الإنسان المتقدم

SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r2.claim: The remaining readers use second-person forms, addressing generic humanity by a shift in person.
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r2.anchor: والباقون بالتاء في الجميع خطابا للإنسان المراد به الجنس على طريق الالتفات

TAB:89:18/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:18/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:18/r1.claim: Qatāda says God rejects the idea that wealth makes a person honored or poverty makes one disgraced; honor comes through obedience and disgrace through disobedience.
TAB:89:18/r1.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  وأمّا إذَا ما ابْتَلاهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيقُولُ رَبّي أهانني

TAB:89:18/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:18/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB:89:18/r2.claim: Another interpretation says the person should praise God in both prosperity and poverty rather than thank Him for wealth but complain about want.
TAB:89:18/r2.anchor: وقالوا :  معنى الكلام :  كلاّ ،   أي لم يكن ينبغي أن يكون هكذا ،   ولكن كان ينبغي أن يحمده

TAB:89:18/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:18/r3.speaker: author
TAB:89:18/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers Qatāda's view because the following verses identify the conduct behind disgrace: failing to honor orphans and urge feeding the poor.
TAB:89:18/r3.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب :  القول الذي ذكرناه عن قتادة ،   لدلالة قوله بَلْ لا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ

TAB-FULL:v24p377#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p377#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p377#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says wealth does not determine honor or poverty humiliation; God honors through obedience and humiliates through disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v24p377#2/r1.anchor: يقول الله جل ثناؤه: كلا إني لا أكرم من أكرمت بكثرة الدنيا، ولا أهين من أهنت بقلتها

TAB-FULL:v24p377#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p377#2/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p377#2/r2.claim: Others say the person should have praised God in both prosperity and poverty rather than praising one and complaining about the other.
TAB-FULL:v24p377#2/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل أنكر جل ثناؤه حمد الإنسان ربه على نعمه دون فقره، وشكواه الفاقة

TAB-FULL:v24p377#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p377#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p377#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers Qatāda's view: the following verses identify neglect of the orphan and hungry as grounds for humiliation, clarifying the opposite ground for honor.
TAB-FULL:v24p377#2/r3.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب: القول الذي ذكرناه عن قتادة لدلالة قوله {بل لا تكرمون اليتيم} [الفجر: 17]

TABATABAI:89:15-18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r7.claim: The rebuke denies that wealth equals honor and poverty equals humiliation: withholding or granting is a test, and their failure to honor orphans and encourage feeding the poor disproves their claim to dignity.
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r7.anchor: ردع لقولهم إن الكرامة هي في الغنى والتنعم، وفي الفقر والفقدان هوان ومذلة

TABATABAI:89:15-18/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r8.claim: The shift from third person to direct address, along with the contrastive “rather,” intensifies the reproach.
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r8.anchor: وفي الإضراب مضافا إلى أصل الردع تقريع ولتشديد هذا التقريع وقع الالتفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

TABATABAI:89:17-22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:17-22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:17-22/r1.claim: Failing to honor an orphan includes depriving younger children of their father’s inheritance and leaving them destitute, as the next verse confirms.
TABATABAI:89:17-22/r1.anchor: فقوله { بل لا تكرمون اليتيم } عدم إكرامه حرمانه من تراث أبيه

ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r5.claim: One reading has lā taḥāḍḍūn; another has lā taḥāḍḍūna concerning urging food for the poor.
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r5.anchor:
(ولا تحضون)
ويقرأ (ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين).

ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r6.claim: They used to consume orphans' property greedily and hastily; the reprimand then says they fail to honor orphans and urge feeding the poor.
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r6.anchor: وكانوا يأكلون أموال اليتامى إسرافا وبدارا فقال

TABRISI:89:29-30/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29-30/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:29-30/r18.claim: The rebuke for neglecting orphans corrects the claim that restricted provision was meant to humiliate: their actual failing is failure to honor the orphan.
TABRISI:89:29-30/r18.anchor: فبين سبحانه أن الإهانة لما ذكره لا لما قالوه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p509/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p509/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p509/r6.claim: Abu Amr reads the following verbs in third-person plural to match the generic, collective “human”; the second-person reading addresses the audience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p509/r6.anchor: أبو عمرو {يكرمون} وما بعدها (¬11) بالياء (¬12)، وذلك أنه لما # تقدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p509/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p509/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p509/r7.claim: Qudama ibn Maz‘un was an orphan in Umayya ibn Khalaf’s care, and Umayya withheld his right.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p509/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل: كان قدامة بن مظعون (¬5) يتيما في حجر أمية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p512/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p512/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p512/r1.claim: “They do not honor the orphan” may mean they neither treat him kindly nor give him his due, or that they withhold his inheritance as their custom; the next inheritance verse supports the second sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p512/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: لا يعرفون صلة اليتيم (¬1). وهذا يحتمل معنيين:

WAHIDI-QT:89:17/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:89:17/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:89:17/r1.claim: The rebuke rejects the disbeliever's assumption and reports their practice of withholding an orphan's rightful inheritance.
WAHIDI-QT:89:17/r1.anchor: ثم رد هذا على الكافر فقال { كلا } أي ليس الأمر كما يظن هذا الكافر { بل لا تكرمون اليتيم } إخبار عما كانوا يفعلونه من ترك توريث اليتيم وحرمانه ما يستحق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:13-17/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:13-17/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:13-17/r7.claim: The correction rejects the disbeliever's assumption; the people abandoned the orphan's inheritance and denied what was due to him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:13-17/r7.anchor: من ترك توريث اليتيم، وحرمانه ما يستحق من الميراث.

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:anmerkung/r1.claim: The whole rebuke also has readings in the third-person plural rather than the second-person plural.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zum gesamten Scheltwort V. 17–20 existieren auch Lesungen in der 3. statt 2. Person Plural

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-18:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-18:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-18:anmerkung/r1.claim: The triad of feeding, orphans, and the poor appears elsewhere in early and middle Meccan passages, including 107:2–3 and 90:11–16.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-18:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Die drei Elemente Speisung – Waise – Armer tauchen in früh- und mittelmekkanischer Zeit u. a. in 107:2.3 und 90:11–16 auf

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:kommentar/r1.claim: The likely later-added verses use the ʾakrama–ʾahāna opposition and echo verse 17's failure to honor orphans, adding an unstable relation to God alongside social sins; other texts name its positive opposite with ṣ-b-r.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:15-16:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die beiden später hinzugefügten (s. o.) Verse 15.16, die terminologisch auf der Opposition

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r1.claim: Verses 17–20 specify the earlier charges against ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh: neglecting help for poor people and orphans, metonymically the vulnerable, and excessive love of possessions.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r1.anchor: Wie in anderen frühmekkanischen Texten werden insbesondere die Unterlassung von Hilfeleistungen gegenüber Armen und Waisen

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r2.claim: These motifs also occur in biblical prophetic books and likely belonged to a literary genre familiar to the hearers.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r2.anchor: Es handelt sich dabei um Motive, die auch in den biblischen Prophetenbüchern präsent sind und wohl auch als Elemente eines den Hörern vertrauten literarischen Genres fungiert haben dürften.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.claim: Passing life’s test requires gratitude for God’s unearned gifts and patience when they are withheld, plus sharing with the poor and vulnerable and encouraging organized social solidarity; Meccan ethics summarize this as reverence for God’s command and compassion for His creatures.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.anchor: bu hususta toplumsal bir duyarlılığın gelişmesine, dayanışma ve yardımlaşmanın kurumsal bir hale gelmesine katkıda bulunmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.claim: The passage sharply criticizes polytheist arrogance, selfish indifference to others, and mad attachment to wealth while teaching Muslims the religious and moral basis for life under God’s will.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.anchor: müşrik Araplar’daki Allah’a karşı küstahlık derecesine kadar varan benlik iddiası, “öteki”ne karşı tam bir sorumsuzluk ve ilgisizliğe götüren egoizm ve çılgınca bir mal tutkusu

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r1.claim: These readers use second-person تاء in تحبون, تكرمون, and تأكلون.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the three verbs in third person with ياء, keeping agreement with the generic, plural الإنسان mentioned earlier.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده بالياء كله .

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r3.claim: A generic plural may be referred to once by grammatical form and elsewhere by its meaning; the passage in al-Aʿrāf illustrates this shift.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r3.anchor: اللفظ، وأخرى على المعنى كقوله: وكم من قرية أهلكناها

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r4.claim: The second-person readings can be understood as an address: tell them this.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتاء فعلى: قل لهم ذلك.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.claim: The verbs addressing the audience and their conduct vary between yāʾ and tāʾ; Kūfan readers alone add an alif in تحاضون. The cited rationale for yāʾ is continuation from the preceding context.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ كلا بل لا تكرمون اليتيم ﴾ ﴿ ولا تحاضون ﴾ و ﴿ يأكلون ﴾

QIRAAT-ER:89:17:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:89:17:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:89:17:4#1/r1.claim: The prefix changes from second-person tu- to third-person yu-, shifting direct address to a report while keeping form and object.
QIRAAT-ER:89:17:4#1/r1.anchor: changes the person prefix from تُـ (tu-, you plural) to يُـ (yu-, they)

ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r1.claim: “No” rebukes and denies both of the person's claims, not merely the second; al-Hasan explicitly supports this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r1.anchor: كلا ردع للإنسان عن قوليه المحكيين وتكذيب له فيهما

ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says neither wealth was given to honor the person nor poverty imposed to disgrace him; both are solely decree and determination.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما المعنى لم أبتله بالغنى لكرامته علي ولم أبتله بالفقر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r3.claim: The address shifts from censuring bad speech to worse conduct; direct address intensifies the rebuke, with the plural referring to humanity as a class.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r3.anchor: وقوله سبحانه بل لا تكرمون اليتيم الخ انتقال وترق من ذمه بالقبيح من القول إلى الأقبح من الفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r4.claim: The rich fail to fulfill the duty created by their wealth: they do not treat orphans kindly and generously.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r4.anchor: حيث يكرمكم الله تعالى بكثرة المال فلا تؤدون ما يلزمكم فيه من إكرام اليتيم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r5.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r5.claim: A prophetic report says the most beloved houses to God are those containing an honored orphan; al-Alusi gives no grading.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث أحب البيوت إلى الله تعالى بيت فيه ينيم مكرم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r6.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r6.claim: Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Abu Rajaʾ, Qatada, al-Jahdari, and Abu ʿAmr read the verb in the third person: “they do not honor.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p126#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد وأبو رجاء وقتادة والجحدري وأبو عمرو لا يكرمون بياء الغيبة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r1.speaker: أهل البصرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r1.claim: Basran readers use third-person yāʾ in the four verbs; others address the audience with tāʾ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل البصرة: "يكرمون، ويحضون، ويأكلون، ويحبون" بالياء فيهن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r2.claim: Failing to honor an orphan means either treating the orphan well inadequately or withholding the orphan’s due.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r2.anchor: لا تحسنون إليه. وقيل: لا تعطونه حقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r3.claim: Muqatil says Qudama b. Mazʿun was an orphan in Umayya b. Khalaf’s care, and Umayya denied him his right.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: كان قدامة بن مظعون يتيما في حجر أمية بن خلف وكان يدفعه عن حقه

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-19/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-19/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-19/r2.claim: Their actual conduct is worse than their mistaken words: they fail to spend compassionately on orphans and do not even urge their families to feed the poor; Kufans read تحاضون.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:15-19/r2.anchor: بل فعلهم أسوأ من قولهم وأدل على تهالكهم بالمال وهو أنهم لا يكرمون اليتيم

BINTSHATI:v2p153/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p153/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p153/r6.claim: These verses connect tyranny and corruption with greed-driven individualism: dishonoring orphans, failing to urge care for the needy, plundering inheritance, and loving wealth until conscience, insight, and the heart are dulled.
BINTSHATI:v2p153/r6.anchor: وبهذا البيان المحكم، ترتبط الآيات التي لفتت ذا حجر إلى مصير الذين طغوا في البلاد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r1.claim: Neither abundance nor scarcity inherently signals honor or humiliation; either can be a trial, punishment, or means of forgiveness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r1.anchor: لا التوسعة منحصرة في الإكرام ولا التضييق منحصر في الإهانة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r2.claim: God may expand provision for a person destined for misery as gradual enticement, or restrict it to honor and turn another from desire.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r2.anchor: وهذا لمن يريد سبحانه به الشقاء فيعجل له طيباته في الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r3.claim: Biqāʿī cites the ṣaḥīḥ report about the bald, leper, and blind men of the Children of Israel as a strong illustration.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r3.anchor: وفي الصحيح في حديث أقرع وأبرص وأعمرى في بني إسرائيل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r4.claim: The real measure of a person's condition is obedience or disobedience, expressed here through treatment of the orphan.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r4.anchor: ذكر أن معيار من جبل على حب الطاعة ومن جبل على حب المعصية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r5.claim: People often refuse to honor or give to orphans because the weak child cannot return a benefit or praise.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r5.anchor: بالإعطاء ونحوه شفقة عليه ورحمة له لأنه ضعيف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r8.claim: The wording first speaks of the human in the singular to generalize, then uses plural verbs to address the human species collectively.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r8.anchor: وأفرد أولا لأنه أنص على التعميم وجمع ثانيا إعلاما بأن المراد الجنس

DURR-FULL:v8p508/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p508/r7.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
DURR-FULL:v8p508/r7.claim: A report says the Prophet recited the following verbs with yāʾ in the reading about honoring the orphan and urging the feeding of the poor.
DURR-FULL:v8p508/r7.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ / بل لا يكرمون اليتيم ولا يحضون / بالياء

TAB:89:17/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:17/r1.claim: Qatada reports the rebuke that people wrongly infer divine honor from wealth and humiliation from poverty.
TAB:89:17/r1.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله : وأما إذا ما ابتلاه فقدر عليه رزقه فيقول ربي أهانني ما أسرع ما كفر ابن آدم

TAB:89:17/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r2.speaker: author
TAB:89:17/r2.claim: The rebuke explains that honor comes through obedience and humiliation through disobedience, not through worldly wealth or poverty.
TAB:89:17/r2.anchor: يقول الله جل ثناؤه : كلا إني لا أكرم من أكرمت بكثرة الدنيا ، ولا أهين من أهنت بقلتها ، ولكن إنما أكرم من أكرمت بطاعتي

TAB:89:17/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB:89:17/r3.claim: Others say God rebukes people for praising Him only for prosperity and complaining about poverty; they should praise Him in both conditions.
TAB:89:17/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل أنكر جل ثناؤه حمد الإنسان ربه على نعمه دون فقره ، وشكواه الفاقة . وقالوا : معنى الكلام : كلا ، أي لم يكن ينبغي أن يكون هكذا

TAB:89:17/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r4.speaker: author
TAB:89:17/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers Qatada’s view because the following verses identify neglecting orphans and the poor as the reason for humiliation, making the cause of honor clear by contrast.
TAB:89:17/r4.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب : القول الذي ذكرناه عن قتادة ، لدلالة قوله بَلْ لا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ والآيات التي بعدها

TAB:89:17/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r5.speaker: author
TAB:89:17/r5.claim: God explains that He humiliated them because they do not honor the orphan and do not urge one another to feed the poor.
TAB:89:17/r5.anchor: بل إنما أهنت من أهنت من أجل أنه لا يكرم اليتيم ، فأخرج الكلام على الخطاب ، فقال : بل لستم تكرمون اليتيم

TAB:89:17/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r6.speaker: author
TAB:89:17/r6.claim: The statement shifts into direct plural address: you do not honor the orphan.
TAB:89:17/r6.anchor: فأخرج الكلام على الخطاب ، فقال : بل لستم تكرمون اليتيم

TAB:89:17/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر وعامة قراء الكوفة
TAB:89:17/r7.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and most Kufan readers use second-person forms and taḥāḍḍūn with an alif, meaning you do not urge one another to feed the poor.
TAB:89:17/r7.anchor: فقرأه من أهل المدينة أبو جعفر وعامة قرّاء الكوفة بَلْ لا تُكْرِمونَ الْيَتيمَ وَلا تَحاضّونَ بالتاء أيضا وفتحها ، وإثبات الألف فيها

TAB:89:17/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r9.speaker: عامة قراء البصرة
TAB:89:17/r9.claim: Basran readers use third-person ya forms and no alif, reporting that those people do not honor the orphan or urge feeding the poor.

TAB:89:17/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r11.speaker: author
TAB:89:17/r11.claim: Al-Tabari regards the three established regional readings as sound in meaning, so a reciter is correct with any of them.
TAB:89:17/r11.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندي : أن هذه قراءات معروفات في قراءة الأمصار ، أعني القراءات الثلاث صحيحات المعاني ، فبأي ذلك قرأ القارىء فمصيب

NASHR:v2p399#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p399#2/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p399#2/r9.claim: The Basrans except al-Zubayrī from Rawḥ read the four verbs in third person; the others, including al-Zubayrī, address the audience directly.
NASHR:v2p399#2/r9.anchor: فقرأ البصريان سوى الزبيري عن روح بالغيب في الأربعة، وقرأ الباقون بالخطاب ومعهم الزبيري عن روح

ABUHAYYAN:89:17/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:17/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:17/r1.claim: Kallā rejects the claim: wealth and restriction are not measures of honor; God honors by enabling piety and humiliates by enabling sin, then exposes their bad conduct.
ABUHAYYAN:89:17/r1.anchor: { كلا } : رد على قولهم ومعتقدهم ، أي ليس إكرام الله وتقدير الرزق سببه ما ذكرتم ، بل إكرامه العبد : تيسيره لتقواه ، وإهانته : تيسيره للمعصية

ABUHAYYAN:89:17/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:17/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:89:17/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says kallā rebukes the claim and bal points to a worse failing: despite receiving wealth, they neglect the required care and kindness toward orphans.
ABUHAYYAN:89:17/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : كلا ردع للإنسان عن قوله ، ثم قال : بل هنا شر من هذا القول ، وهو أن الله تعالى يكرمهم بكثرة المال ، فلا يؤدون فيها ما يلزمهم من إكرام اليتيم

ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r2.speaker: الحديث
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r2.claim: A hadith says the most beloved home to God is one in which an orphan is treated honorably; no grading is stated.
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث : « أحب البيوت إلى الله تعالى بيت فيه يتيم مكرم »

ALUSI:89:17/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:17/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:17/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes and falsifies both reported judgments about wealth and poverty, not just the second; al-Ḥasan explicitly supports this reading.
ALUSI:89:17/r1.anchor: ردع للإنسان عن قوليه المحكيين وتكذيب له فيهما لا عن الأخير فقط

ALUSI:89:17/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:17/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:89:17/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says wealth is not a test of God's honoring a person, nor poverty a test of His humiliating him; both follow sheer decree and destiny.
ALUSI:89:17/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما المعنى لم أبتله بالغنى لكرامته على ولم أبتله بالفقر لهوانه على

ALUSI:89:17/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:17/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:17/r3.claim: Bal escalates from reproach for a bad statement to a worse deed; the shift to direct address intensifies rebuke and censure.
ALUSI:89:17/r3.anchor: انتقال وترق من ذمه بالقبيح من القول إلى الأقبح من الفعل والالتفات إلى الخطاب لتشديد التقريع

ALUSI:89:17/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:17/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:89:17/r4.claim: An alternative supplies an implied qul, so there is no grammatical shift of address, though the wording still signals their degradation.
ALUSI:89:17/r4.anchor: وقيل هو بتقدير قل فلا التفات نعم فيه من الإشارة إلى تنقيصهم ما فيه

ALUSI:89:17/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:17/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:17/r5.claim: The plural address treats al-insān as a collective genus and accuses them of worse conduct and greed: despite receiving wealth, they fail in required kindness and care for orphans.
ALUSI:89:17/r5.anchor: والجمع باعتبار معنى الإنسان إذا المراد هو الجنس أي بل لكن أفعال وأحوال أشد شرا مما ذكر

ALUSI:89:17/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:17/r6.speaker: حديث
ALUSI:89:17/r6.claim: A hadith says the houses most beloved to God are those containing an honored orphan; al-Ālūsī gives no transmitter or grading here.
ALUSI:89:17/r6.anchor: أحب البيوت إلى الله بيت فيه يتيم مكرم

ALUSI:89:17/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:17/r7.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو رجاء وقتادة والجحدري وأبو عمرو
ALUSI:89:17/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Abū Rajaʾ, Qatāda, al-Jaḥdarī, and Abū ʿAmr read the verb in third-person form, lā yukrimūna.
ALUSI:89:17/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد وأبو رجاء وقتادة والجحدري وأبو عمرو لا يكرمون بياء الغيبة

BAGHAWI:89:17/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:17/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:89:17/r5.claim: The rebuke denies that abundant provision proves divine favor or that poverty proves divine contempt.
BAGHAWI:89:17/r5.anchor: فرد الله على من ظن أن سعة الرزق إكرام وأن الفقر إهانة ،   فقال : { كلا } لم أبتله بالغني لكرامته

BAGHAWI:89:17/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:17/r6.speaker: أهل البصرة
BAGHAWI:89:17/r6.claim: Basra reads the four verbs about honoring, urging, eating, and loving in the third person with yāʾ; the other readers use second-person tāʾ.
BAGHAWI:89:17/r6.anchor: قرأ أهل لبصرة :  "  يكرمون ،   ويحضون ،   ويأكلون ،   ويحبون "  بالياء فيهن ،   وقرأ الآخرون بالتاء

BAGHAWI:89:17/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:17/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:89:17/r7.claim: The rebuke means that they do not treat the orphan well; another explanation is that they withhold the orphan's due.
BAGHAWI:89:17/r7.anchor: لا تحسنون إليه .   وقيل : لا تعطونه حقه .   قال مقاتل : كان قدامة بن مظعون يتيماً

BAGHAWI:89:17/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:17/r8.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI:89:17/r8.claim: Muqatil says Qudama ibn Mazun was an orphan in Umayya ibn Khalaf's care, and Umayya denied him his right.
BAGHAWI:89:17/r8.anchor: قال مقاتل : كان قدامة بن مظعون يتيماً في حجر أمية بن خلف وكان يدفعه عن حقه

BAYDAWI:89:17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:17/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes both claims; expansion is a divine favor, but restricting provision is not itself humiliation, since the verse says “measured” rather than “humiliated.”
BAYDAWI:89:17/r1.anchor: مع أن قوله الأول مطابق لأكرمه ولم يقل فأهانه وقدر عليه كما قال فأكرمه ونعمه

BAYDAWI:89:17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:17/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
BAYDAWI:89:17/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads the final yāʾ of akramanī and ahānanī without it in both pause and continuation; the Kūfans do likewise, as does Abū ʿAmr, while Nāfiʿ does so at pause.
BAYDAWI:89:17/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر والكوفيون أكرمن وأهانن بغير ياء في الوصل والوقف وعن أبي عمرو مثله

BAYDAWI:89:17/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:17/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
BAYDAWI:89:17/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads qaddara with a doubled dāl.

BAYDAWI:89:17/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:17/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:17/r4.claim: The people are reproached for failing to honor the orphan.

BAYDAWI:89:20/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:20/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAYDAWI:89:20/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Sahl, and Yaʿqūb read the relevant verbs from “do not honor” through “love” in the third-person masculine; the others use second-person forms.
BAYDAWI:89:20/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وسهل ويعقوب لا يكرمون إلى ويحبون بالياء والباقون بالتاء

BIQAI:89:17/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:17/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:17/r1.claim: It rebukes the shallow inference that poverty means humiliation and wealth means honor: either condition may lead to happiness or misery, and worldly expansion often accompanies misery.
BIQAI:89:17/r1.anchor: فإن الإقتار قد يؤدي إلى سعادة الدارين

BIQAI:89:17/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:17/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:17/r2.claim: God neither honors simply by increasing worldly goods nor humiliates simply by reducing them; disobedience brings humiliation, sometimes through prosperity as a snare and sometimes through constriction that expiates sin.
BIQAI:89:17/r2.anchor: لا أكرم بتكثير الدنيا ولا أهين بتقليلها

BIQAI:89:17/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:17/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:17/r3.claim: The author cites the sound report about the bald man, leper, and blind man among the Israelites as a strong witness that worldly prosperity and restriction do not straightforwardly signify honor or humiliation.
BIQAI:89:17/r3.anchor: وفي الصحيح في حديث أقرع وأبرص وأعمى في بني إسرائيل

BIQAI:89:17/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:17/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:17/r4.claim: Instead, people's disobedience and attachment to worldly things explain the pattern: God may expand provision for the doomed as a snare or restrict it for others as honor, restraint from desire, and a return to kindness toward the weak.
BIQAI:89:17/r4.anchor: فيوسع على بعض من جبل على الشقاء إهانة له بالاستدراج

BIQAI:89:17/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:17/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:17/r5.claim: A criterion distinguishing people disposed to obedience from those disposed to sin is their aversion to or love of worldly life.
BIQAI:89:17/r5.anchor: معيار من جبل على حب الطاعة ومن جبل على حب المعصية بغض الدنيا وحبها

BIQAI:89:17/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:17/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:17/r6.claim: Most people fail to honor orphans through giving and similar care, despite the orphan's vulnerability and lack of expected benefit or praise in return.
BIQAI:89:17/r6.anchor: بالإعطاء ونحوه شفقة عليه ورحمة له لأنه ضعيف

DURR:89:15/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:15/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR:89:15/r1.claim: Hasan says both claims are false: wealth does not prove God honored a person, nor poverty that He humiliated them; the following verse instead identifies their real disgrace as failing to honor orphans.
DURR:89:15/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : { فأما الإِنسان } الآية

DURR:89:15/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:15/r3.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:15/r3.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf reports that the Prophet recited the following clauses with yāʾ (third-person plural); al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR:89:15/r3.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ { بل لا يكرمون اليتيم

DURR:89:16/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:16/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR:89:16/r1.claim: Hasan says both claims are false: wealth does not prove God honored a person, nor poverty that He humiliated them; the following verse instead identifies their real disgrace as failing to honor orphans.
DURR:89:16/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : { فأما الإِنسان } الآية

DURR:89:16/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:16/r3.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:16/r3.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf reports that the Prophet recited the following clauses with yāʾ (third-person plural); al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR:89:16/r3.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ { بل لا يكرمون اليتيم

DURR:89:20/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r13.speaker: عاصم
DURR:89:20/r13.claim: Asim reads the clauses with second-person tāʾ in tukrimūn, taḥāḍḍūn (lengthened and unhamzated), and taʾ in turath, with lamman geminated.
DURR:89:20/r13.anchor: عن عاصم رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ { كلا بل لا تكرمون اليتيم } بالتاء ورفع التاء { ولا تحاضون } ممدودة

DURR:89:20/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r14.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:20/r14.claim: Abu Hurayra says the Prophet read all four clauses with yāʾ, in the third-person plural.
DURR:89:20/r14.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ { كلا بل لا يكرمون اليتيم

DURR:89:20/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r15.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:20/r15.claim: Ibn Umar likewise reports the Prophet reading the clauses through 'they love wealth' with yāʾ throughout.
DURR:89:20/r15.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ

IBNASHUR:89:16/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:16/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:16/r10.claim: Kallā rebukes both claims: worldly conditions do not prove a person’s standing with God; His intent is known through revelation rather than ordinary appearances.
IBNASHUR:89:16/r10.anchor: فهو ردع عن اعتقاد ذلك فمناط الردع كلا القولين لأن كل قول منهما صادر عن تأول باطل

IBNASHUR:89:16/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:16/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:16/r12.claim: A person may be prosperous yet displeasing to God, while a disheveled, rejected poor person may be so favored that an oath on God’s behalf would be fulfilled.
IBNASHUR:89:16/r12.anchor: فرب رجل في نعمة في الدنيا هو مسخوط عليه ورب أشعث أغبر مطرود بالأبواب

IBNASHUR:89:16/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:16/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:16/r13.claim: Kallā rejects the inference that prosperity signals approval or poverty signals humiliation, not the fact that God bestows worldly benefits; disbelievers are humiliated in the afterlife.
IBNASHUR:89:16/r13.anchor: وليس مناطه وقوع الكرامة ووقوع الإهانة لأن الله أهان الكافر بعذاب الآخرة

IBNASHUR:89:16/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:16/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:16/r14.claim: If disbelief itself caused worldly humiliation through restricted provision, every unbeliever would be poor; thus poverty is not the sign being refuted.
IBNASHUR:89:16/r14.anchor: ولو شاء إهانته في الدنيا لأجل الكفر لأهان جميع الكفرة بتقتير الرزق

IBNASHUR:89:16/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:16/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:16/r15.claim: There is no contradiction between God granting actual benefits and kallā, because kallā rejects the claim that those benefits prove divine approval.
IBNASHUR:89:16/r15.anchor: لأن الإبطال وارد على ما قصده

IBNASHUR:89:16/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:16/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:16/r16.claim: God’s dealings have causes and purposes beyond ignorant conjecture; people should seek evidence through reason and revelation without forcing conclusions.
IBNASHUR:89:16/r16.anchor: أن لشأن الله في معاملته الناس في هذا العالم أسراراً وعللاً

IBNASHUR:89:16/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:16/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:16/r17.claim: People of knowledge place matters correctly and infer from guidance rather than confusing or misapplying evidence.
IBNASHUR:89:16/r17.anchor: وأما أهل العلم فهم يضعون الأشياء مواضعها

IBNASHUR:89:17/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:17/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:17/r1.claim: Bal is a transitional shift, linked by contrast to the supposed honor of wealth: although they boast of divine favor, they fail to honor God’s servants.

IBNASHUR:89:17/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:17/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:17/r2.claim: They withhold surplus wealth from those in need while seeking more than they need, refuting their pride in generosity.
IBNASHUR:89:17/r2.anchor: إذ حرموا أهل الحاجة من فضول أموالهم وإذ يستزيدون من المال ما لا يحتاجون إليه

IBNASHUR:89:17/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:17/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:17/r3.claim: The orphan statement is a new sentence, either opening discourse or parenthetically separating the two kallā statements.
IBNASHUR:89:17/r3.anchor: فجملة : { لا تكرمون اليتيم } استئناف كما يقتضيه الإضراب

IBNASHUR:89:17/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:17/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:17/r4.claim: Honoring an orphan means meeting his needs and treating him kindly, since he has lost his provider and may be vulnerable around inherited property.

IBNASHUR:89:17/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:17/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:17/r5.claim: Yatīm is a child whose father has died; the generic definite form means orphans collectively.

IBNASHUR:89:17/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:17/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:17/r6.claim: Kallā rebukes the notion that prosperity or restricted provision results from God intending to honor or humiliate a person.
IBNASHUR:89:17/r6.anchor: { كلا } ردع عن هذا القول أي ليس ابتلاء الله

IBNASHUR:89:17/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:17/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:17/r7.claim: This general rebuke is left unexplained because the conclusion about God watching over the earlier nations already summarizes their fate.
IBNASHUR:89:17/r7.anchor: وهذا ردع مجمل لم يتعرض القرآن لتبيينه اكتفاء بتذييل أحوال الأمم الثلاث

IBNASHUR:89:18/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:18/r5.claim: Reciprocal implication supplies omitted complements: not honoring orphans entails not urging their guardians to honor them; not urging food entails not feeding the poor from one’s wealth.
IBNASHUR:89:18/r5.anchor: وقد حصل في الآية احتباك لأنهم لما نفي إكرامهم اليتيم وقوبل بنفي أن يحضوا على طعام المسكين

IBNASHUR:89:18/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r8.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR:89:18/r8.claim: Most readers use second-person forms, shifting from the earlier third-person framing to confront the audience with a more forceful rebuke.
IBNASHUR:89:18/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : « لا تكرمون ، ولا تحضون ، وتأكلون ، وتحبون » بالمثناة الفوقية على الخطاب

IBNASHUR:89:18/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
IBNASHUR:89:18/r9.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb read the verbs in third person, informing the Prophet and believers of the audience’s conduct, as in the cited passage.
IBNASHUR:89:18/r9.anchor: وقرأها أبو عمرو ويعقوب بالمثناة التحتية على الغيبة لتعريف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمسلمين بذلك

IBNATIYYA:89:17/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:17/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:89:17/r1.claim: Kallā rejects their belief: wealth and poverty are tests; the wealthy should thank and obey, the poor should be grateful and patient, and honor comes through piety while humiliation comes through sin.
IBNATIYYA:89:17/r1.anchor: ثم قال تعالى : { كلا } ردّاً على قولهم ومعتقدهم

IBNATIYYA:89:17/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:17/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:89:17/r2.claim: A human orphan is one who has lost his father before reaching maturity; an animal orphan has lost its mother.
IBNATIYYA:89:17/r2.anchor: وهو من بني آدم الذي فقد أباه وكان غير بالغ

IBNATIYYA:89:17/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:17/r3.speaker: عمر
IBNATIYYA:89:17/r3.claim: The Prophet says the most beloved homes to God are those containing an honored orphan; al-Suyuti marks the report sound.
IBNATIYYA:89:17/r3.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : «أحَبُّ البيوت إلى الله

IBNKATHIR:89:17/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:17/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:17/r1.claim: The assumption that wealth proves honor and poverty proves humiliation is false: God gives or withholds wealth from those He loves and those He does not; the duty is gratitude when rich and patience when poor.
IBNKATHIR:89:17/r1.anchor: فإن الله يعطي المال من يحب ومن لا يحب ، ويضيق على من يحب ومن لا يحب

IBNKATHIR:89:17/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:17/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:17/r2.claim: The verse commands people to treat the orphan with honor.
IBNKATHIR:89:17/r2.anchor: وقوله : { بَل لا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ } فيه أمر بالإكرام له

IBNKATHIR:89:17/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:17/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR:89:17/r3.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the best Muslim home has an orphan treated well and the worst has one treated badly; the Prophet says he and the orphan’s caretaker will be together in Paradise, gesturing with his fingers.
IBNKATHIR:89:17/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : " خير بيت في المسلمين بيت فيه يتيم يحسن إليه

IBNKATHIR:89:17/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:17/r4.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR:89:17/r4.claim: Sahl ibn Saʿd reports the Prophet’s promise that he and the caretaker of an orphan are like these two fingers in Paradise: the middle and index fingers.
IBNKATHIR:89:17/r4.anchor: عن سهل - يعني ابن سعد - أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : " أنا وكافل اليتيم كهاتين في الجنة "

KASHSHAF:89:17/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:17/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:17/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes the human's claim and introduces conduct worse than that claim.
KASHSHAF:89:17/r1.anchor: كَلاَّ } ردع للإنسان عن قوله : ثم قال : بل هناك شر من القول

KASHSHAF:89:17/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:17/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:17/r2.claim: Although God grants abundant wealth, they fail to fulfill its obligation by attending to the orphan and treating the orphan kindly.
KASHSHAF:89:17/r2.anchor: فلا يؤدون ما يلزمهم فيه من إكرام اليتيم بالتفقد والمبرة

KASHSHAF:89:17/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:17/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:17/r5.claim: The verbs here and what follows are read in either third person, “they,” or second person, “you.”

NASAFI:89:17/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:17/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:17/r1.claim: There is a worse fault than misreading wealth as honor: although God enriches them, they fail to fulfill the duty of treating orphans kindly.
NASAFI:89:17/r1.anchor: بل هناك شر من هذا القول وهو أن الله يكرمهم بالغنى فلا يؤدون ما يلزمهم فيه

NASAFI:89:18/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:18/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:18/r1.claim: There is a worse fault than misreading wealth as honor: although God enriches them, they fail to fulfill the duty of treating orphans kindly.
NASAFI:89:18/r1.anchor: بل هناك شر من هذا القول وهو أن الله يكرمهم بالغنى فلا يؤدون ما يلزمهم فيه

NASAFI:89:20/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:20/r4.speaker: البصري
NASAFI:89:20/r4.claim: The Basran reading uses third-person forms yukrimun, yahuddun, ya’kulun, and yuhibbun for the corresponding second-person forms in verses 17–20.
NASAFI:89:20/r4.anchor: { يكرمون } { وَلاَ يحضون } { وَيَأْكُلُونَ } { وَّيُحِبُّونَ } بصري

QURTUBI:89:17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:17/r1.claim: كلا rejects the assumption that wealth proves favor or poverty proves disgrace; both poverty and wealth follow God's decree.
QURTUBI:89:17/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : " كلا " ردّ ، أي ليس الأمر كما يظن ، فليس الغنى لفضله ، ولا الفقر لهوانه ، وإنما الفقر والغنى من تقديري وقضائي

QURTUBI:89:17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:17/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:89:17/r2.claim: Al-Farra says كلا means a servant should not behave this way, but should praise God in both prosperity and poverty.
QURTUBI:89:17/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء : " كلا " في هذا الموضع بمعنى لم يكن ينبغي للعبد أن يكون هكذا ، ولكن يحمد اللّه عز وجل على الغنى والفقر

QURTUBI:89:17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:17/r3.speaker: حديث قدسي
QURTUBI:89:17/r3.claim: A divine saying denies that worldly abundance is God's honor or scarcity His humiliation, defining honor by obedience and disgrace by disobedience.
QURTUBI:89:17/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( يقول اللّه عز وجل : كلا إني لا أكرم من أكرمت بكثرة الدنيا ، ولا أهين من أهنت بقلتها ، إنما أكرم من أكرمت بطاعتي

QURTUBI:89:17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:17/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:17/r4.claim: They failed to honor orphans by withholding inheritance and consuming their property wastefully and hastily before they grew up.
QURTUBI:89:17/r4.anchor: " بل لا تكرمون اليتيم " إخبار عن ما كانوا يصنعونه من منع اليتيم الميراث ، وأكل ماله إسرافا وبدارا أن يكبروا

QURTUBI:89:17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:17/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
QURTUBI:89:17/r5.claim: Abu Amr and Yaqub read the four verbs with yāʾ, treating the preceding human as a collective expressed in plural form.

QURTUBI:89:17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:17/r6.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI:89:17/r6.claim: The other readers use tāʾ in all four verbs, addressing the audience directly as a rebuke.
QURTUBI:89:17/r6.anchor: الباقون بالتاء في الأربعة ، على الخطاب والمواجهة ، كأنه قال لهم ذلك تقريعا وتوبيخا

QURTUBI:89:17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:17/r7.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI:89:17/r7.claim: Muqatil says the verse was revealed about Qudama ibn Mazun, an orphan under the guardianship of Umayya ibn Khalaf.
QURTUBI:89:17/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل : نزلت في قدامة بن مظعون وكان يتيما في حجر أمية بن خلف

RAZI:89:17/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:89:17/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes the claim that worldly wealth proves honor or poverty proves contempt; God's allocation is not such a verdict.
RAZI:89:17/r1.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما حكى عنهم تلك الشبهة قال : { كلا }

RAZI:89:17/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:89:17/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God does not test someone with riches because He honors him or with poverty because He despises him.
RAZI:89:17/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : المعنى لم ابتله بالغنى لكرامته علي

RAZI:89:17/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r3.speaker: أهل السنة
RAZI:89:17/r3.claim: On the Sunni account presented here, allocation follows sheer decree, power, will, and judgment, which transcend causal explanations.
RAZI:89:17/r3.anchor: بل ذلك إما على مذهب أهل السنة ، فمن محض القضاء

RAZI:89:17/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:89:17/r4.claim: On the Muʿtazilite account, allocation follows hidden benefits that only God can know.
RAZI:89:17/r4.anchor: وإما على مذهب المعتزلة فبسبب مصالح خفية لا يطلع عليها إلا هو

RAZI:89:17/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:89:17/r5.claim: God may expand an unbeliever's wealth without honoring him or restrict a believer without despising him.
RAZI:89:17/r5.anchor: فقد يوسع على الكافر لا لكرامته

RAZI:89:17/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:89:17/r6.claim: The people's conduct is worse than their mistaken claim: God gives them abundant wealth, yet they fail to honor the orphan.
RAZI:89:17/r6.anchor: فكأنه قال : بل لهم فعل هو شر من هذا القول

RAZI:89:17/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI:89:17/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads this and the following verbs in the third person, matching al-insān as a collective, third-person expression.
RAZI:89:17/r7.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو : { يكرمون } وما بعده بالياء المنقوطة من تحت

RAZI:89:17/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:89:17/r8.claim: The second-person reading is addressed by the Prophet to the people: 'Say this to them.'
RAZI:89:17/r8.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتاء فالتقدير قل لهم يا محمد ذلك

RAZI:89:17/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r9.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:89:17/r9.claim: Muqātil reports that Qudāma ibn Maẓʿūn was an orphan in the care of Umayya ibn Khalaf, who withheld his right.
RAZI:89:17/r9.anchor: قال مقاتل : كان قدامة بن مظعون يتيما في حجر أمية بن خلف

RAZI:89:17/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:89:17/r10.claim: One form of failing to honor the orphan is neglecting kindness toward him, connected with the failure to urge feeding the poor.
RAZI:89:17/r10.anchor: ترك بره ، وإليه الإشارة بقوله : { ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين }

RAZI:89:17/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:89:17/r11.claim: A second form is withholding the orphan's inheritance and consuming his property, connected with devouring the estate.
RAZI:89:17/r11.anchor: دفعه عن حقه الثابت له في الميراث وأكل ماله

RAZI:89:17/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:17/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:89:17/r12.claim: A third form is taking the orphan's money and joining it to one's own wealth.
RAZI:89:17/r12.anchor: أي تأخذون أموال اليتامى وتضمونها إلى أموالكم
